speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to begin our assessment, have you been experiencing pain, stiffness, or a popping sensation when the swelling started?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Panner's Disease (or Osteochondrosis of the Capitellum). Given the age (18 months), trauma-free onset of swelling after activity, and positive family history, this is consistent with a self-limiting osteochondrosis affecting the lateral elbow/knee equivalent. No further tests are required at this time.
